title: Microsoft Purview: OCR scans images embedded in Office files and PDFs in SharePoint and OneDrive
summary: Hold for corrections to the SharePoint automation guidance and the claim that no budget setting is documented. The current PowerShell reference describes the selected-sites parameter and requires SelectedSites scope; Azure Cost Management documents budgets that can monitor the billing subscription but do not stop consumption.

claims.quote: With Embedded support, OCR will scan content in DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and PDFs (scanned and hybrid containing searchable text and images). This will be in addition to support for standalone images

claims.claim: Until now, a policy looking for credit card numbers or classification markings read the text of a file rather than embedded image text.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Optical character recognition (OCR) reaches the location and group configuration page.
claims.quote:
Select Settings.
3. Select Optical character recognition (OCR) to enter your OCR configuration settings.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API for the Purview tenant OCR location and group settings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR settings locations groups Security Compliance PowerShell Graph API; Security & Compliance OCR PowerShell settings. Read Purview OCR and returned references; SharePoint parameters and Communication Compliance OCR are different controls.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center path through Pay-as-you-go services and Optical character recognition reaches site selection at Edit.
claims.quote: On the Optical character recognition panel, under Select the SharePoint libraries where you would like to enable optical character recognition, select Edit.
claims.fix: Extend the existing path after 'Edit' with ' > Enable optical character recognition in Microsoft 365 > All sites / Selected sites (up to 100) / No sites'. The current path is correct but stops before the scope options.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -OpticalCharacterRecognitionSelectedSitesList <String[]> sets which SharePoint sites OCR runs on without a stated scope prerequisite.
claims.quote: This parameter can only be called if optical character recognition's scope is set to SelectedSites. The inputted list of site URLs cannot exceed 100 items.
claims.fix: Keep the call but qualify its note: 'Requires pay-as-you-go billing and OCR scope already set to SelectedSites. Supply up to 100 SharePoint site URLs; this call overwrites the existing selected-sites list by default.' The parameter does not select All sites or No sites.

claims.claim: The Set-SPOTenant reference lists OpticalCharacterRecognitionSelectedSitesList and its type without describing it.
claims.quote: This parameter allows administrators to pass a list of SharePoint site URLs to modify the optical character recognition premium feature's selected sites list. By default this parameter overwrites the existing list with the user input list.
claims.fix: Remove both statements that the parameter is undescribed. Replace the prose with 'The Set-SPOTenant reference documents -OpticalCharacterRecognitionSelectedSitesList as replacing the selected-sites list with up to 100 site URLs; it requires OCR scope SelectedSites and pay-as-you-go billing.'

claims.claim: The site scope panel offers All sites, Selected sites with a maximum of 100, or No sites.
claims.quote: On the Enable optical character recognition in Microsoft 365 panel, change the setting from All sites to Selected sites (up to 100) or No sites.

claims.claim: Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services > Billing > Document processing services reaches the billing configuration.
claims.quote: On the Services tab, select Pay-as-you-go services.
claims.fix: Use 'Settings > Org settings > Services > Pay-as-you-go services > Billing > Document processing services > Set up billing and turn on services > Set up billing > Azure subscription'. This restores the services-list tab and extends the route to the subscription control.

claims.claim: No API for connecting the document processing billing subscription is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: document processing pay as you go billing connect subscription PowerShell REST API; Syntex billing PowerShell subscription; document processing billing Graph subscription API. Opened syntex-azure-billing; found portal instructions, not a connection API.

claims.claim: The billing page separately documents disconnecting the Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Under Manage billing, select Disconnect Azure subscription.

claims.claim: If service and DLP site lists differ, the documented maximum number of sites is enabled for OCR.
claims.quote: If there are different sites specified for the service and data loss prevention, the maximum number of sites will be enabled for OCR.

claims.claim: Specifying sites in both service and DLP configuration does not cause a double processing charge.
claims.quote: You won't be charged twice for processing.

claims.claim: Supported image formats include BMP, PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, HEIC and raw camera formats.
claims.quote: BMP, PNG, JPEG, JPG, JFIF, ARW, CR2, CRW, ERF, GIF, MEF, MRW, NEF, NRW, ORF, PEF, RAW, RW2, RW1, SR2, TIF, TIFF, HEIC, HEIF

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to inventory policies, review Cost Management and consider backfill, but these controls have no corresponding rows.
claims.quote: List the DLP, records management and insider risk policies ... Review Microsoft Cost Management for Azure ... Decide whether existing content needs the backfill cmdlet
claims.fix: The policy-inventory, Cost Management and backfill checklist steps have no control rows. Remove these checklist bullets to align the checklist with the existing table; this correction does not require adding rows.

claims.claim: The briefing presents documented Purview OCR behaviour without noting that another Microsoft page still calls its settings preview.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview includes OCR (preview) settings for Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management, Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention, Microsoft Purview Data Loss Management, and auto-labeling.
claims.fix: Add: 'The Purview OCR page does not mark these settings preview, but the Communication Compliance policy documentation still calls the shared Purview OCR settings preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-policies#policy-settings.
